comparison: Perfect alignment on background claims (C1-C8). Both evaluations support the rationale, biological context, and framing of the research question. Reviewers described the study as 'timely' and accepted the background as appropriate motivation for the systematic review.

Both support the study selection process (C9-C11), though peer review R1 covers broader scope including study characteristics (C12-C27). OpenEval provides detailed validation of PRISMA methodology, while peer reviewers affirmed adherence to 'expected systematic review and meta-analysis standards' and described work as 'high-quality.'

Both support study characteristics (C12-C17). OpenEval emphasizes critical limitations (male-only animals, no comorbidities) for translational validity. Peer reviewers accepted these descriptive findings within their broader endorsement of systematic review standards.

Both support intervention characteristics (C18-C27). OpenEval provides detailed validation of heterogeneity documentation and timing contextualization. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings as part of their overall endorsement of the systematic review quality.

Perfect alignment on patient-prioritized outcome gaps (C28-C29). Both evaluations support this as a key finding. Peer reviewers specifically highlighted patient engagement as 'an outstanding feature' and accepted the identification of evidence gaps relative to patient priorities.

Perfect alignment on cerebroprotective meta-analysis results (C30-C36). Both evaluations strongly support these findings. OpenEval validates statistical methodology and heterogeneity management. Peer reviewers stated 'the presented evidence is convincing' and 'overall results were promising.'

Both support behavioral outcome findings (C37-C40). OpenEval notes appropriate documentation of limitations. Peer reviewers described results as 'promising' and noted the study 'adds substantially to the evidence base,' accepting reported effects despite acknowledged heterogeneity.

Both support nuanced behavioral synthesis (C41-C48). OpenEval emphasizes critical confounding issues (non-equivalent infarct volumes). Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of their assessment that results 'adds substantially to the evidence base.'

Both support risk of bias assessment (C49-C54). OpenEval validates systematic assessment showing high prevalence of reporting issues. Peer reviewers acknowledged 'some shortcomings regarding guideline adherence,' accepting the authors' critical evaluation.

Both address qualification criteria (C55-C59), but OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN while peer review is SUPPORTED. OpenEval questions whether criteria were truly satisfied given critical confounders (temperature, early histology). Peer reviewers accepted the STAIR/SRRR assessment with acknowledgment of 'some shortcomings.'

Both support identification of critical limitations for CAMAROS trial (C60-C62). OpenEval emphasizes baseline infarct volume confounding and dosing discrepancy. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this translational gap analysis, describing work as 'timely' and noting it 'adds substantially to the evidence base.'

Both support systematic documentation of translational validity gaps (C63-C69, C70). OpenEval provides detailed validation against STAIR/SRRR criteria. Peer reviewers specifically praised the assessment of 'adherence to current quality assurance guidelines' as 'another important feature.'

Both support PRIMED tool assessment (C70). OpenEval validates this as independent confirmation of translational readiness evaluation. Peer reviewers accepted the systematic evaluation approach using established guidelines.

Both support balanced summary of evidence (C71-C76). OpenEval emphasizes differential strength across outcome domains. Peer reviewers aligned with this nuanced interpretation, noting 'overall results were promising' while acknowledging 'some shortcomings.'

Perfect alignment on meta-analysis methodology discussion (C77-C80). Both support the authors' sophisticated handling of preclinical heterogeneity. Peer reviewers stated authors 'adhered to expected standards' and 'provided good academic justification' for methodological decisions.

Both support synthesis of risk of bias implications (C81-C83). OpenEval emphasizes association with effect overestimation. Peer reviewers accepted the critical assessment, acknowledging 'some shortcomings regarding guideline adherence.'

Both support balanced assessment of evidence quality and gaps (C84-C86). OpenEval characterizes as 'good initial evidence' with extensive qualifications. Peer reviewers described work as 'important' and noted it 'adds substantially to the evidence base.'

Both address trial-relevant evidence (C87-C94), but OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN while peer review is SUPPORTED. OpenEval questions whether single experiment with methodological limitations constitutes robust 'proof of concept.' Peer reviewers accepted the assessment, describing work as 'timely' with 'good academic justification.'

Strong alignment on methodological innovations (C95-C97). Both strongly support patient engagement and STAIR/SRRR framework use. Peer reviewers explicitly praised patient participation as 'an outstanding feature' that 'goes beyond established standards.'

Both support balanced conclusions (C98-C102). OpenEval validates the appropriately nuanced interpretation acknowledging promise and limitations. Peer reviewers aligned, noting results were 'promising' while work 'goes beyond established standards' in critical evaluation.

Both support recommendations for integrating STAIR/SRRR guidance (C101-C102). OpenEval emphasizes methodological contribution. Peer reviewers praised the approach as going 'beyond established standards.'

Strong alignment on comprehensive methodology (C103-C120). Both strongly support adherence to systematic review best practices. OpenEval provides detailed validation of each methodological component. Peer reviewers explicitly stated authors 'adhered to expected standards' and praised 'extremely detailed and transparent supplements.'

Both support patient engagement methodology (C103-C106). OpenEval validates robust involvement throughout research process. Peer reviewers specifically highlighted this as 'an outstanding feature' that is 'hardly realized in research practice.'
